001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation;
002
003import static java.lang.annotation.RetentionPolicy.CLASS;
004
005import java.lang.annotation.Documented;
006import java.lang.annotation.ElementType;
007import java.lang.annotation.Retention;
008import java.lang.annotation.Target;
009
010// @formatter:off
011/**
012 * Used to generate Rainbow Gum config builder objects that once built will call the
013 * method annotated with the properties from the generated builder on build. The method
014 * annotated is essentially a factory method that a builder will be generated to configure
015 * each parameter in the factory method. The build call on the builder will call the
016 * annotated factory method.
017 * <p>
018 * While there exist many annotation processors that generate builders (Immutables for
019 * example) the builders generated by this annotation (and corresponding processor) are
020 * LogProperties aware such that the builder can extract its arguments from LogProperties.
021 * <p>
022 * Here is an example:
023 * {@snippet :
024class final SomeFactory {
025        @LogConfigurable(name="MyPluginBuilder", prefix="logging.myplugin.{name}.")
026        static MyPlugin of(@KeyParameter String name, Integer myParameter) {
027                // do some additional logic.
028                return new MyPlugin(name, myParameter);
029        }
030 }
031 * }
032 * The above will create a builder called <code>MyPluginBuilder</code> with a setter of
033 * <code>myParameter</code> and its constructor will take a String name argument.
034 * {@snippet :
035 * MyPlugin plugin = new MyPluginBuilder("example").myParameter(80).fromProperties(properties).build();
036 * }
037 * The builder will try the property <code>logging.myplugin.example.myParameter</code> and
038 * use it if it exists to override the <code>80</code> value.
039 * <p>
040 * If the annotated factory method throws {@link IllegalArgumentException} (or a
041 * subclass), the generated builder's <code>build()</code> treats that as a validation
042 * failure: it is caught and rewrapped as a
043 * <code>io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogProperty.ValidationException</code>, the same exception
044 * a per-property conversion failure produces. This is the way to validate a relationship
045 * <em>between</em> multiple parameters (for example, one field's valid range depending on
046 * another field's value) that a single property's own conversion can't catch by itself.
047 * Prefer naming the specific parameter(s) at fault in the exception's message, since that
048 * message becomes the body of the resulting <code>ValidationException</code> as-is:
049 * {@snippet :
050class final SomeFactory {
051        @LogConfigurable(name="MyPluginBuilder", prefix="logging.myplugin.{name}.")
052        static MyPlugin of(@KeyParameter String name, int min, int max) {
053                if (min > max) {
054                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("min (" + min + ") must not be greater than max (" + max + ")");
055                }
056                return new MyPlugin(name, min, max);
057        }
058 }
059 * }
060 * <p>
061 * If constructing the target type needs something only available on
062 * {@code io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogConfig} itself (for example another component that can
063 * only be resolved once config exists), prefer returning
064 * {@code io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogProvider<MyPlugin>} from the factory method instead of
065 * <code>MyPlugin</code> directly:
066 * {@snippet :
067class final SomeFactory {
068        @LogConfigurable(name="MyPluginBuilder", prefix="logging.myplugin.{name}.")
069        static LogProvider<MyPlugin> of(@KeyParameter String name, Integer myParameter) {
070                // still validate/parse everything derivable from properties eagerly, right here.
071                return (n, config) -> new MyPlugin(name, myParameter, config);
072        }
073 }
074 * }
075 * The factory method still runs (and can still throw {@link IllegalArgumentException})
076 * as soon as the builder is built; only the part of construction that genuinely needs
077 * {@code LogConfig} is deferred, to whenever <code>provide(name, config)</code> is
078 * actually called later.
079 */
080// @formatter:on
081@Retention(CLASS)
082@Target({ ElementType.CONSTRUCTOR, ElementType.METHOD })
083@Documented
084public @interface LogConfigurable {
085
086        /**
087         * Name of builder.
088         * @return name of builder by default if not set Builder will be suffixed to
089         * targetType.
090         */
091        String name() default "";
092
093        /**
094         * Property prefix to use for property lookup. Usually these come from LogProperties
095         * string constants and have a parameter of "name". If the prefix has parameters they
096         * can be specified with {@link KeyParameter} as arguments on the static factory
097         * method.
098         * <p>
099         * An example might be: "logging.component.{name}." which has a parameter of "name".
100         * @return prefix in general should end in ".".
101         * @see KeyParameter
102         */
103        String prefix();
104
105        /**
106         * Use as parameter to property keys with parameters. This annotation should only be
107         * used on String arguments and the builder will require it as an initial constructor
108         * argument to avoid it being missing.
109         */
110        @Retention(CLASS)
111        @Target({ ElementType.PARAMETER })
112        @Documented
113        public @interface KeyParameter {
114
115                /**
116                 * Use as parameter to a property name specified in
117                 * {@link LogConfigurable#prefix()}. An example is a parameter called
118                 * <code>name</code> with a prefix like <code>logging.myplugin.{name}.</code>
119                 * @return by default will use the parameter name.
120                 */
121                String value() default "";
122
123        }
124
125        /**
126         * Use to set static defaults to parameters.
127         */
128        @Retention(CLASS)
129        @Target({ ElementType.PARAMETER })
130        @Documented
131        public @interface DefaultParameter {
132
133                /**
134                 * Will use use a static field on the factory class (the class that contains the
135                 * annotated {@link LogConfigurable} method) as a default value if missing from
136                 * properties or not set.
137                 * @return by default will use the static field
138                 * <code>DEFAULT_parameterName</code>.
139                 */
140                String value() default "";
141
142        }
143
144        /**
145         * Wall call a static method on the factory class (the class that contains the
146         * annotated {@link LogConfigurable} method) with the property value as a string to be
147         * converted.
148         * <p>
149         * The annotated method is only called when the property is actually present - if the
150         * property is missing and the parameter is optional (nullable or has a default), the
151         * generated builder resolves straight to <code>null</code>/the default without ever
152         * calling the converter, so it never needs to handle a missing or <code>null</code>
153         * raw value itself.
154         */
155        @Retention(CLASS)
156        @Target({ ElementType.PARAMETER })
157        @Documented
158        public @interface ConvertParameter {
159
160                /**
161                 * Static method on target type to call to convert the parameter. The method must
162                 * be return a type and have a single argument.
163                 * @return static method name.
164                 */
165                String value();
166
167        }
168
169        /**
170         * A parameter not to be configured with properties that will just pass through to the
171         * build method.
172         */
173        @Retention(CLASS)
174        @Target({ ElementType.PARAMETER })
175        @Documented
176        public @interface PassThroughParameter {
177
178        }
179
180}
